decisions: Historical production hunks allow an exact-digest but unsigned recovery directive to terminalize a signed intent, clear a durable pending restart, and remove quarantine. They treat Aborted as terminal and allow later different grants; the added same-digest replay guard only addresses that newly admitted state.

Current recover_signed_intent intentionally accepts only Committed or RolledBack as terminal; other states remain or become RecoveryRequired and fence runtime. apply_production_transition also refuses every non-Committed/non-RolledBack signed intent, including an Aborted record. Thus no clean lease absence or successful kill can auto-authorize a legacy unsigned abort or replay its grant.

The current explicit resolve_production_recovery API requires a RecoveryRequired intent and release transaction, matching grant, registered release-binding digests, lifecycle and authority epoch, and a verify_recovery-validated independent signature with exact signer, time validity and all digest bindings. The historical unsigned directive would bypass this contract even if its digest is current.

Keep the complete current production implementation. Preserve the historical stale-directive rejection test already present. The old positive auto-abort test is intentionally superseded by the current matching-unsigned-directive rejection and repeated-cold-recovery tests, preserving exact intent, directive, inactivity and quarantine. No test is skipped or gate relaxed.

decisions: The historical hunk adds a Mutex held over all evaluate_expression calls solely to prevent the initial Windows sandbox allocator pool from racing; it adds no tests and leaves production concurrency unchanged.

Current initialize_v8 performs drop(v8::new_default_allocator()) inside INIT.call_once after platform and V8 initialization. Every evaluate_expression calls initialize_v8 before creating its isolate; the Once completion synchronizes all later smoke calls with the allocator initialization.

The exact locked v8 150.4.0 implementation proves this call reaches the intended lazy state: Rust new_default_allocator -> binding.cc v8__ArrayBuffer__Allocator__NewDefaultAllocator -> api.cc NewDefaultAllocator -> ArrayBufferAllocator constructor -> IsolateGroup::GetSandboxedArrayBufferAllocator -> backend_allocator_.LazyInitialize(sandbox()).

With partition allocation, LazyInitialize constructs impl_ on first use without its own mutex; executing it once before parallel calls prevents that first-use race. The backend lives in the default IsolateGroup and the wrapper owns only pointers, so dropping the wrapper does not tear down the initialized backend. The non-partition backend also initializes under its own mutex. Keep current localized initialization and all original smoke assertions instead of serializing evaluation.
This is source-level equivalence for the stated lazy-initialization problem. It is not a claim that Windows V8 binaries or the complete platform matrix passed in this environment.
